title: Woundness and the central p-torsion kernel condition
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G,U,F$ be $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Affine algebraic means affine of finite type, and unipotence and scalar extension have the meanings of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. Smoothness means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness means [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbb A^1_k=\mathbf G_a$ as a $k$-scheme [def-sc-gm-ga]. A group $G$ is $k$-wound if it is smooth, connected, affine algebraic and unipotent, and every morphism of $k$-schemes $f:\mathbb A^1_k\to G$ factors as the structure map $\mathbb A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ followed by a point $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$. For a natural number $p$ and a homomorphism $i:F\to U$, the smooth connected central $p$-torsion subgroup condition means that $F$ is affine algebraic, $i$ is a closed subgroup inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], $F$ is smooth and connected, every $F(A)$-point maps into the universal centre of $U(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ (the centralizer of the identity subgroup, in [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]), and $x^p=1$ for every $x\in F(A)$. The cckp-kernel condition on $i$ means that it satisfies this condition and that for every homomorphism $j:B\to U$ satisfying the same condition there is a group-scheme homomorphism $f:B\to F$ with $i\circ f=j$. In characteristic $p>0$ with $p$ prime these are the woundness and cckp-kernel notions of Conrad's Definitions 2.1 and 3.1.

source.place: Conrad (2014), Definition 2.1, printed p.10, and Definition 3.1, printed p.15; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/appbnew.pdf.
